gappers.catalyst: New Seeking Alpha rating-upgrade piece ("Bloom Energy Could See An AI-Memory-Style Frenzy"), second consecutive AI-power-demand catalyst after last week's double-upgrade note
gappers.catalyst_detail: Seeking Alpha published a new bullish rating-upgrade article today ("Bloom Energy Could See An AI-Memory-Style Frenzy"), building directly on last week's "Bloom Energy Just Won Another Catalyst" double-upgrade piece -- part of a steady stream of 10+ bullish SA notes over the past month. This is BE's second consecutive pre-market gap on the same AI-power-demand thesis (this morning's 08:15 ET scan already flagged a +14.14% gap on the same narrative); the stock has now extended further, from Thursday Sep 4's close of $252.87 (+7.35%) to ~$270-273 pre-market.
gappers.why: AI data centers face a power-delivery bottleneck (grid interconnect queues run 3-5+ years); Bloom's on-site solid-oxide fuel cells deploy in months without grid dependency, making it a direct beneficiary of the AI-power-shortage trade. A fresh bullish research note comparing BE's setup to the AI-memory (HBM) re-rating frenzy adds a new narrative hook pulling in momentum/theme buyers on top of already-strong fundamentals and an already-extended move.
gappers.impact: Increasingly extended, multi-session move rather than a single-day spike -- today's gap builds on this morning's earlier +14.14% print, both on rating-upgrade narrative rather than new fundamental data (no earnings, no new contract since Thu Sep 4's report). More likely to be a genuine multi-day momentum run given persistence across two scans today, but also more vulnerable to a sharp mean-reversion given how far above an already rich valuation (285x+ trailing PE per this morning's research) it has pushed. Sector read-through: still part of the same AI-infra/power risk-on cluster as NBIS/CRWV/RGTI moving the same morning.
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM, lean short-term: still no hard fundamental trigger today (no earnings, no new contract, just a second rating-upgrade note riding existing momentum), even though the underlying AI-power-demand thesis is structurally LONG_TERM.
gappers.opportunity_cost: At ~$273 a 10% trailing stop is ~$27/share of risk; clearing 2:1 R:R needs a stretch target near $327, tougher now than at this morning's $268 print given the stock has run further intraday. Chasing a name already flagged and extended once today conflicts with TRADING-STRATEGY.md's no-chase rule (no entry within 3% of a print already up >5% on the day). Would also eat into the 3-new-trades/week cap and 20%-per-position ceiling versus a less-extended entry; RGTI's confirmed, discrete government quantum-stake news remains a cleaner setup among today's gappers.

gappers.catalyst_detail: Unlike this morning's 08:15 ET scan (which found no dated, company-specific driver for NBIS), this run surfaced a fresh same-day item: Stocktwits reported ("NBIS Stock Jumps After Palantir, Nebius Team Up to Let Companies Own Their AI Models, Not Rent Them", published roughly 30-50 minutes before this scan) that Palantir and Nebius announced a partnership around AI-model ownership. This layers on Nebius's existing hyperscaler narrative -- a $17.4B multi-year Microsoft compute contract and Nvidia's 9.3% equity stake -- and the dilution overhang from its mid-August $4.5B convertible-note raise.
gappers.why: NBIS is one of the highest-beta "neocloud" plays on AI compute demand; a named strategic partner (Palantir) and a differentiated "own not rent" AI-model positioning gives NBIS a discrete, company-specific news hook today rather than pure sector beta, amplified by NBIS's smaller float and rich valuation (~122x sales per this morning's research) when the broader AI-infra trade is risk-on.
gappers.impact: More sustainable read than this morning's assessment, given a same-day, dated, company-specific announcement (Palantir tie-up) rather than unconfirmed sector momentum alone. Still carries the dilution overhang from the August convertible offering, and valuation remains stretched. Sector-wide participation continues (ORCL/CRWV/RGTI also gapping this morning) -- a real risk-on rotation day for the AI-infra theme, not a single-name flash.
gappers.horizon: LONG_TERM lean, upgraded from this morning's SHORT_TERM call: a named strategic partnership, if it holds up under further reporting, is a more structural catalyst than yesterday's unconfirmed momentum and aligns with the early-cycle Technology favor in TRADING-STRATEGY.md's sector-rotation table -- still needs Confluence-rule confirmation (2+ of VWAP/RSI/200-SMA/insider) on a later /trade check before treating it as more than a headline pop.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Run scripts/corr-gate.mjs before any entry -- NBIS is highly correlated with CRWV (same theme, same-day movers), and Confluence rule argues for at most one of the two. At $231 a 10% stop is ~$23/share risk, needing ~$277 to clear 2:1 R:R, plausible only if the Palantir tie-up thesis proves durable beyond today's pop. Competes with BE/CRWV/RGTI for the same 6-position cap and 3-trades/week limit.

gappers.impact: Mixed-to-cautious: today's move looks like sector beta (moving WITH Oracle, not on its own news) layered on already-known bearish undercurrents (insider selling, flagged this morning) now reinforced by a same-day bond-market-skepticism piece questioning the credit quality behind the touted $100B backlog. gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM, same lean as this morning: no discrete CRWV catalyst today, riding sector/Oracle sympathy; the fresh credit-skepticism piece is an additional caution flag, not a reason to upgrade horizon.

gappers.catalyst: Pre-earnings analyst target raises (Morgan Stanley, Mizuho) ahead of Thursday Sep 10 fiscal Q1 FY27 report -- NOT an earnings beat itself; report is still 2 days out
gappers.catalyst_detail: Verified: Oracle's fiscal Q1 FY27 earnings are scheduled AFTER MARKET CLOSE this Thursday, September 10 (confirmed via Oracle's own Sep 2 press release and multiple outlets) -- today's +8.2% pre-market gap is NOT earnings-driven, it is pre-earnings positioning. Morgan Stanley raised its price target to $210 (from $207) while staying "cautious" per the headline, and Mizuho published a note arguing "100% upside" heading into the print; the stock had already closed Thu Sep 4 up 3.08% and continued climbing into results day. 24/7 Wall St flagged CoreWeave (CRWV) advancing 3% today in the same story, i.e. Oracle's rally is also the proximate driver for part of CRWV's move.
gappers.why: Anticipatory momentum ahead of a binary, scheduled earnings event -- analyst target raises and bullish pre-earnings notes pull in momentum buyers positioning for an AI-cloud-driven beat, not confirmation of one. Oracle's forward P/E (~19.7x) is far cheaper than the neocloud names (NBIS/CRWV run >100x sales), giving it a fundamentally different valuation and catalyst mechanism from the rest of today's AI-infra cluster despite sharing the AI theme.
gappers.impact: Different sustainability question than BE/NBIS/CRWV: this is a $457B mega-cap with real, profitable financials (26.75% net margin, ~$17B TTM net income, 27x trailing P/E) gapping into a KNOWN, dated catalyst rather than a headline-driven neocloud pop. Today's move can fully reverse Thursday/Friday on the actual print in either direction -- elevated event risk, not a stable AI-power/AI-infra momentum read-through. Sector read-through: pulls CRWV up in sympathy today, but is mechanistically distinct (real scheduled earnings event vs. neocloud backlog/momentum narrative).
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM, tightly bound to the Sep 10 earnings date: any position taken today faces a binary reprice within 48 hours regardless of direction; not a swing-hold setup until the print is known.
gappers.opportunity_cost: Entering ORCL now means holding through a scheduled earnings gap-risk event within the week -- conflicts with TRADING-STRATEGY.md's no-chase guardrail (no entry within 3% of a print already up >5% on the day) and its documented-catalyst requirement (today's move is analyst-target-raise speculation, not a confirmed fundamental print). A 10% trailing stop (~$17/share) could be blown through cleanly by an earnings-day gap in either direction. Would also compete with the AI-infra cluster (BE/NBIS/CRWV/RGTI) for the 6-position cap; a cleaner alternative is to wait for Thursday's print and react to confirmed results rather than pre-position into known binary risk.

gappers.catalyst: Gapping DOWN with the broader crypto-equity complex (MSTR, COIN, CRCL) after Bitcoin's rejection at $82K; BMNR is an ETHEREUM-treasury company (correcting the working assumption it holds bitcoin)
gappers.catalyst_detail: Correction to the working assumption: BMNR (BitMine Immersion Technologies) is an ETH treasury company, not a bitcoin-treasury company -- confirmed via BMNR's own press release today announcing ETH holdings reached 5.93 million tokens (up from 5.74M in prior reporting) with total crypto + cash of $15.7B. Today's -6.2% gap tracks a broader, same-day crypto-equity pullback: Stocktwits reports "MSTR, COIN, CRCL Stocks Dip: Crypto Equities Pull Back After Bitcoin's $82K Rejection." BMNR was up 46.5% in August (Nasdaq) and had been recovering toward $17.50-18 resistance in prior TradingView coverage before today's pullback, so this also reads partly as profit-taking after a large recent run.
gappers.why: BMNR's price is driven by (1) its NAV-per-share tied to ETH holdings and (2) broad crypto-market risk sentiment; a Bitcoin rejection at a key level ($82K) triggers basket-wide de-risking across crypto-treasury/crypto-exposed equities (MSTR, COIN, CRCL, BMNR) regardless of each company's specific underlying asset (BTC vs ETH) -- this is correlated sector selling, not a BMNR-specific negative development.
gappers.impact: Reads as a sector-wide risk-off pullback in crypto-linked equities rather than a BMNR-specific problem -- the underlying ETH-accumulation story is intact and arguably strengthening (5.93M tokens, up from 5.74M). Pre-market volume of 1.73M shares is the HIGHEST of today's 6 gappers, consistent with a broad, high-participation de-risking move rather than a thin/noisy print. Sector read-through: correlates with the MSTR/COIN/CRCL crypto-equity basket, a wholly different cluster from the AI-infra names (BE/NBIS/CRWV/RGTI) gapping UP today.
gappers.horizon: SHORT_TERM: tied to Bitcoin's intraday level around $82K; a BTC bounce would likely reverse this move quickly given BMNR's high-beta NAV-tracking behavior, but continued BTC weakness could extend the pullback. No structural BMNR-specific negative found.
gappers.opportunity_cost: This is a DOWN gap, not a long-entry candidate -- TRADING-STRATEGY.md's no-bottom-fish rule ("no long entry without a documented catalyst; drawdown alone is not a catalyst") and stocks-only/long-bias framing both argue against treating this as a new-trade setup today. Relevant only if BMNR is an existing open position, in which case this pullback should be checked against the -7% manual-cut and 10% trailing-stop rules rather than added to; not a new-trade candidate either way given the down-gap.
